proofs.description:
The simulating machine `simMachine M₀` performs one transition per `TM0` transition and one more
for halting, so it decides within `T + 1 ≤ 1 · (T + |w| + 1)` steps (`singleTape_simulation_succ`).

The stack machine `tm R idIn idOut` simulates `R` (`TM2Sim.simulate`) within
`30 (|x| + T) + 30` steps for `T = C (|x| + 1)^d`, a polynomial in `|x|`.

Fix `k = K + 1 ≥ 3` and compile the counter implicit parity system `counter K ℓ` (main
location carrying all `2^{(k-1)ℓ}` counter values, three equality schemas per increment
position, endpoints initialized `0` and `1`) with the row-space compiler.

* Its conflict round `τ` is finite and at least `2^{(k-1)ℓ}` (`counter_conflictRound`, via
  a potential argument along the chain of equalities).
* Its size parameter is at most `C_K 2^ℓ` (`sizeParameter_le`): the coordinates of the
  domain of an increment at position `j` have fixed bits in the rows below `⌊j/K⌋`, which
  bounds both the domain size and the rank of the restricted check matrix.
* Duplicator survives `τ - 1` rounds of the bijective `(k+1)`-pebble game, so the graphs have
  equal size `n` and, by the game characterization, every distinguishing round `r` satisfies
  `τ ≤ r + k`; Spoiler wins eventually, so `k`-WL distinguishes the graphs.
* Hence `n^{k-1} ≤ (C C_K 2^ℓ)^{k-1} ≤ (C C_K)^{k-1} τ ≤ (C C_K)^{k-1}(k+1) r`.
* Since `k`-WL distinguishes two graphs after at most `2 n^k` rounds if at all
  (`exists_distinguishesAfter_le`), `τ ≤ 2 n^k + k`, so choosing `ℓ` large forces `n ≥ n₀`.

We show that `k`-WL already distinguishes `G` and `H` after exactly `r` rounds. Otherwise
all round-`r` color classes have equal sizes, so `|V(G)| = |V(H)|`, and Duplicator survives
`r` rounds with the invariant that, for every pebble Spoiler may lift, the remaining placed
pebble pairs lie on two `k`-tuples with equal round-`s` colors (`s` the number of remaining
rounds). Equality of round-`(s+1)` colors yields a bijection matching the substituted color
tuples, which keeps the new state a partial isomorphism (using `k ≥ 2`) and, via the
invariance of colors under reindexing tuples, re-establishes the invariant.

Combination of the two directions: a distinction after `r` rounds gives a Spoiler win
within `r + k` rounds, and if no round distinguishes `G` and `H`, Duplicator survives every
number of rounds.

If the vertex numbers differ Spoiler wins at once. Otherwise Spoiler uses the first `k`
rounds to place pebbles `0, …, k-1` one by one, always choosing a vertex for which the
number of extensions of the placed prefix with a fixed round-`r` color differs between `G`
and `H`; this ends in tuples with different round-`r` colors. From such tuples Spoiler wins
within `r` more rounds by induction: he places the free pebble on a vertex where the
substituted color tuples differ under Duplicator's bijection and continues with the
`k` pebbles carrying a pair of tuples with different round-`(r-1)` colors.

Let `L ∈ DTIME(2^n) \ DTIME(2^{n/4})` be decided by `M` within `C₀ 2^n + C₀` steps, and
put `c₀ = 2 C₀ + 2`. For `|x| = n ≥ 2`, `h = n + c₀`, `a = ⌈log₂(n + 2)⌉` and `s` the least
number with `s a ≥ h + 2`, a machine computes `encodeNats [h, s] ++ x` in time `O(m^3)`
(`m = n + c₀ + 4`), and the pipeline turns it in time `m^{O(1)}` into an instance
`(s + 1, G₀, G₁)` of length `N ≤ B m^5` (`exp_len_arith`), which `(s+1)`-WL distinguishes iff
`x ∈ L`. With `ε = 1 / (4 (B + 1)^{1/5})`, a decider for WL Distinguishing within
`C 2^{ε N^{1/5}} + C` steps runs within `C 2^{m/4} + C` steps on these instances; together
with the polynomial reduction this decides `L` in time `O(2^{n/4})`, a contradiction.

For `L ∈ EXPTIME`, a deterministic decider (from `singleTape_simulation`) is run on padded
inputs `true :: true :: x` (`padded_decides`); the machine `redTM R d` writes
`encodeNats [h, h] ++ true :: true :: x` with `h = 2^(d (|bits n| + 1)) - 1` and runs the
pipeline machine `R` of `pipeline_language`. The choice `d = A + D + B + 2` (from the
coefficient sum `A` and degree `D` of the polynomial and the constant `B` of the decider)
gives `h ≥ p(n) + n + B`, so the decider halts within `2^h` steps, while
`h + 1 ≤ (4 (n + 1))^d` and `2^ℓ ≤ 8 (n + 1)` make the running time polynomial. The machine
is translated by `tm2_of_polyTime`.

For `P ∈ XP` with decider `M` in time `f(k) (n + 1)^{f(k)}`, let `F k = 2 f(k) + 4`. The
reduction machine `padTM Q` writes the padded input `y = true :: true :: x` and runs `Q`, the
composition of `withSuffix` of the machine of `xpS` (which computes `[h, s]` with
`h = F(k) ⌈log₂ (|x| + 4)⌉` and `s = F(k) + 1`, `xp_prog`) with the pipeline machine
(`pipeline_language`) of the padded decider. The padded decider halts within
`(|x| + 4)^{F k} ≤ 2^h` steps (`xp_halt_arith`), so the pipeline is correct; its running time
is polynomial in `|x|` with a degree independent of `k`, since the block width is at most
`⌈log₂ (|x| + 4)⌉ + 1` (`xp_width_le`, `xp_total_arith`). The new parameter is
`s + 1 = 2 f(k) + 6`.

A diagonal argument. The diagonal machine computes a clock of `2^n` units on inputs of length
`n` by doubling a unary counter `n` times (in time `O(2^n)`), and runs the universal stack
program under this clock; the universal program answers the negation of the machine whose code
is a prefix of the input. So the diagonal language is in `DTIME(2^n)`. The universal program
has cubic overhead: simulating `T` steps on inputs of length `n` costs `O(n^2 T^3)` (with a
constant depending on the simulated machine). A machine running within `C 2^{n/4} + C` steps is
thus simulated within `O(n^2 2^{3n/4}) ≤ 2^n` steps on long inputs `code M ++ 0^k`, where the
diagonal machine answers differently.

The proof uses translation (padding) to reduce the claim to a coarse hierarchy:
`DTIME(n^{3b+3})` is not contained in `DTIME(n^b)`. The coarse hierarchy follows from a
diagonal argument. A universal stack program simulates the machine whose code is a prefix of
the input, with polynomial overhead, under a clock of `n^{3b+3}` steps. The case `s = 1` is
handled directly: a machine running in time `o(n)` cannot read the last input bit.

(→) is the witness theorem `witness_from_rounds`: a distinction after `r` rounds yields a colored
graph of treewidth at most `k` with different homomorphism counts.

(←) Let `F` have treewidth at most `k`, and take a one-vertex tree decomposition of width `k` of
it (Abramsky–Jakl–Paine): a rooted forest on `V(F)` where each vertex `v` has a bag of at most
`k + 1` vertices containing `v`, the rest of which lies in the bag of the parent, and every edge
lies in a bag. A map `V(F) → V(G)` is a homomorphism if and only if every vertex satisfies its
local condition (color, and edges to the rest of its bag). Counting the maps on the subtree of a
vertex `c`, with the vertices outside given, yields the recursion "choose the image `x` of `c`,
check the local condition at `c`, and multiply the counts for the children of `c`". By induction
from the leaves, the count for `c` is a function of the round-`r` WL color (for some `r`) of the
`k`-tuple formed by images of labels `ℓ` covering the rest of the bag of `c`: the sum over `x`
is a WL refinement step, in which every child either keeps the labels `ℓ` or replaces one
position (not needed for the rest of its bag; it exists since that rest has at most `k - 1`
vertices besides `c`) by `c`. At a root, the count is a sum over all `k`-tuples of a
WL-determined function, so it agrees for `G` and `H` when no round of `k`-WL distinguishes them;
`hom(F, ·)` is the product of these counts over the roots.

Put `M = |V(G)|^k + |V(H)|^k`, the number of `k`-tuples of `G` and `H`. Labeled graphs carry
edges, color predicates, equality constraints and `k` labels; a good one has a rooted bag tree
of width `k` with all labels in the root bag. By induction on `r`, each round-`r` color-class
indicator of `k`-WL on `V(G)^k ⊔ V(H)^k` is a linear combination of tensors of good labeled
graphs with at most `ν_r` vertices besides the labels, where `ν_0 = 0` and
`ν_{r+1} = (M - 1)(1 + k ν_r)`: round zero and the step both use polynomial closure (degree at
most `M - 1`), with atoms for equalities, edges and colors in round zero, and gluing and
extension for the step. Applying the functional "sum over `V(G)^k` minus sum over `V(H)^k`" to
the indicator of a class of different sizes gives a good labeled graph with different
homomorphism counts into `G` and `H`. Taking the quotient by the equality constraints,
excluding loops, symmetrizing edges and splitting by the colorings compatible with the
predicates yields a colored graph of treewidth at most `k` with at most
`k + ν_r ≤ k (k M)^r` vertices distinguishing `G` and `H`.

For `k ≥ 3` and `ε > 0`, assume a
deterministic machine decides `k`-WL distinguishability within `C N^{k-1-ε} + C` steps on
encoded pairs of length `N`. With `s = k - 1` and `ε' = min ε 1`, the time hierarchy theorem
gives a language `L ∈ DTIME(n^s) \ DTIME(n^{s - ε'/2})`. The reduction maps inputs of length
`n ≥ 2` in time `t₁ = O(n log^c n)` to encoded graph pairs of length `N ≤ t₁` that `k`-WL
distinguishes exactly for members of `L`. Running the reduction, rewinding, and then the fast
decider (and answering inputs of length `< 2` directly) decides `L` within
`2 t₁ + O(t₁^{k-1-ε'}) + O(1) = O(n^{s - ε'/2})` steps, contradicting the choice of `L`.

The construction is the pair of explicit matrix graphs, with vertices listed in the order
`ordL I` produced by the compiler machine and colors the position of the first vertex of a
class (`Compiler.compileM`): Spoiler follows a derivation of the conflict backwards through the
strips with row sweeps, Duplicator maintains seed descriptions with coefficient bits repaired in
an untouched repetition, the size bound counts the vertex list and the edge bound uses that
every edge contains a hub of degree at most three (`Compiler.reGraph_spec`). Colors and edge
endpoints are numbers below `3 |V|`, so the encoding has length `O((S + 1) log (S + 2))`
(`Compiler.length_out_le_log`). The construction time is witnessed by the counter-machine program
`prog p4Sch` (`Compiler/Prog`): the passes `P0`–`P3` compute the location and schema data
and the answers of the join, `P4` emits both graph descriptions, its schema edge part
`p4Sch` meeting the interface `SchSpec` with linear cost (`p4Sch_spec`); the program is
compiled to a Turing machine running in time `O((H + S) log³ (H + S + 2))`.

The system is `Iv M x s ℓ H` (the compiled code-ordered verifier program), with `ℓ` the
packed width and `H = max(h, ℓ) ≤ h + 1`; its correctness and the `O((h + 1)^2)` bounds on
locations and schemas are `packed_bounds_h`. The machine is the composition of the preprocessor
`pkPre` (`pkPre_computesWithin`: it reads `h, s` and writes the input as records of `16`
symbols carrying `x_k` and the flags `[k < |x|], [k < h], [k < s]`, in time
`O((2^ℓ + h) (h + 1)^2)`) and the machine of the packed generator `redGenP M`
(`redGenP_computesWithin`): a generator in the stack language `Gn` whose loops over blocks and
registers run up to runtime values, analysed with growth classes on two scales (`2^ℓ`
times a factor `O(h)` for the input length and the register values, and `(h + 3)^2` for the
linear quantities), in time `O(2^ℓ (h + 1)^37)`.

The explicit graphs `rsGraph I 0` and `rsGraph I 1` (vertices: class names with effective
labels, colors an injective code of the class) witness the row-space compiler with the
absolute constant `20` and `Cₖ = (4k + 1)(k + 2) + 6k`. Spoiler follows a derivation of the
conflict backwards, sweeping the `k + 2` stages of every strip with the mask vertices
(`spoilerWins`); Duplicator maintains seed descriptions whose masks are repaired in a stage
without pebbled mask class (`duplicatorSurvives`); the size bound counts the vertex classes and
labels, with `2^{rank B_e}` masks per stage (`card_names_le`). For item (4), a graph of
treewidth at most `k` has a one-vertex tree decomposition (Abramsky–Jakl–Paine,
`oneVertexForest_of_treewidth`); by the affine dichotomy it has no homomorphism to `G₁`, so the
tree-like linear system of exposed equations along the decomposition is unsolvable (local
realization), and it yields a contradiction tree (`pattern_tree`).

We follow Döring and Neuen and take `C = 13`. Let `k = m + 2`, let `G` have `n` vertices,
and suppose `k`-WL does not stabilize after any of the rounds `0, …, r - 1`, i.e.
`χ_0 ≻ χ_1 ≻ … ≻ χ_r`. It suffices to show `r ≤ 3 n^(k-2) + 10 n^(k-1)`, which is
`< 13 n^(k-1) + 1`.

The colorings `χ_i` are refining, compatible with equality and shufflable for every
`σ : [k] → [k]`. For `v ∈ V^(k-2)` let `χ^v_i (a, b) = χ_i (v, a, b)` and let `⟨χ^v_i⟩` be the
space of complex `n × n` matrices constant on the color classes of `χ^v_i`. Then
`ℂ 1, ⟨χ^v_0⟩, ⟨χ^v_1⟩, …` is a weak chain: it contains the identity (compatibility with
equality), is closed under conjugate transposition (shufflability), and
`⟨χ^v_i⟩ ⟨χ^v_i⟩ ⊆ ⟨χ^v_{i+1}⟩` (Lemma 6.2: an entry of a product is a count over the multiset
part of the next color). Since `⟨χ^v_i⟩ = ⟨χ^v_{i+1}⟩` forces `χ^v_i ≡ χ^v_{i+1}` (Lemma 4.7),
the two-dimensional bound (Theorem 5.15, at most `10 n` strict steps of a weak chain in
`M_n(ℂ)`) bounds the number of rounds `i` with `χ^v_i ≻ χ^v_{i+1}` by `10 n`.

For `k = 2` the only `v` is empty and `χ^v_i = χ_i`, so `r ≤ 10 n`. For `k ≥ 3` let
`χ̄_i (v) = χ_i (v, v_{k-2}, v_{k-2})`. Extendability (Lemma 6.4) and shufflability give
Claim 6.5: if `χ_i (v, w_1, w_2)` is not a color `χ_i (v', ·, ·)`, then
`χ̄_{i+2} (v) ≠ χ̄_{i+2} (v')`. Claim 6.6: if `χ_i ≻ χ_{i+1}` is witnessed by
`(v, a, b)`, `(v', c, d)` and no `χ^w` splits in round `i + 1`, then
`χ̄_i (v) = χ̄_i (v')` (shufflability) and, by Claim 6.5 at round `i + 1`,
`χ̄_{i+3} (v) ≠ χ̄_{i+3} (v')`; so `χ̄` splits in round `i + 1`, `i + 2` or `i + 3`.
Every `χ̄` split increases the number of classes of `χ̄`, which is at most `n^(k-2)`. Taking
